summary: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists a Providence County fire tower on Cato Hill as gone; no other source was found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone. No source describes the tower or the site today.

evidence.supports: Cato Hill is in Providence County, at 42.00533, -71.51565, and is marked gone
The list gives each tower a county, coordinates, a type and a status
evidence.quote: Name County Lat Long Type Status NHLR/FFLOS

notes_for_editor: Single source: one row in the FFLA Rhode Island list. The list gives no build date, height, agency, use or fate, and the NHLR/FFLOS column is blank, so the story is short (about 55 words) rather than padded, below the 120-word target. Two leads, neither used because nothing read ties them to Cato Hill: (a) the Cato Hill Historic District, a residential district in central Woonsocket per a Wikipedia search snippet (page not read); the listed coordinates appear to fall in Woonsocket by a rough check, not a map source. (b) FFLOS 'Woonsocket Tower Site' (US 1553, RI 10, Providence County, no coordinates, wooden tower 1936-1938 replaced by the Durfee Hill Tower). Check against Woonsocket fire history before linking. A search snippet also mentions a Woonsocket Fire Department tower on Boyden Street, which is not Cato Hill; not used. No photos found.
